subject: general
question: Where is the centre of curvature of a convex mirror located?

options.text: At the principal focus of the mirror
At the pole of the mirror

solution: The correct answer is __**Behind the mirror**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **centre of curvature** of a convex mirror is the center of the sphere from which the mirror is a part. • In the case of a **convex mirror**, the reflective surface bulges outward, and the center of the sphere lies **behind the mirror**. • The **centre of curvature** is not located on the reflective side of the convex mirror but rather on the side opposite to the reflection. • This is because all the normals to the surface of a convex mirror point away from the center of curvature. • In a **convex mirror**, the **focal point** and the center of curvature are both virtual, meaning they cannot be physically located in front of the mirror but are positioned behind it.
